chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Musa ibn Imran al-Baghdadi narrated to us, from Ibn Sinan, from Awn ibn Ma'yn, the cap seller, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: I heard al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), say:
The one who meets people with one face and is absent from them with another face, will come on the Day of Resurrection whilst having two tongues of fire.

key_terms.غَابَهُمْ: was absent from them (metaphor for inner reality or true self)
key_terms.وَجْهٍ: face (metaphor for outward appearance or demeanor)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for hypocrisy according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s warning that hypocrisy results in a physical manifestation of inner duality on the Day of Resurrection, where the 'two tongues of fire' symbolize the punishment for those whose external demeanor contradicts their internal state. This concept of *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) is distinguished from true hypocrisy (*Nifaq*), as the latter involves a deliberate concealment of disbelief or falsehood behind a facade of piety, leading to a specific torment that mirrors the deceit practiced in life.
